subsystems.name: Sensing array
subsystems.role: measures blood flow and skin temperature continuously.
parts: green and infrared LEDs with photodiodes (PPG)

subsystems.name: Electronics
subsystems.role: processes sensor signals and communicates wirelessly.

subsystems.name: Power
subsystems.role: stores enough energy to run for several days between charges.

subsystems.name: Enclosure
subsystems.role: protects the electronics and stays comfortable against skin.

subsystems.name: Firmware and algorithms
subsystems.role: turns raw sensor data into heart rate, HRV, sleep stages and temperature trends.

buildSteps.title: Define the form factor and sensor placement
buildSteps.detail: Engineers choose a ring size and shape that keeps LEDs and photodiodes pressed against the artery on the underside of the finger without causing discomfort.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the flexible circuit board
buildSteps.detail: A curved or rigid-flex printed circuit board is made so the electronics can fit inside the ring's narrow interior.

buildSteps.title: Integrate the battery
buildSteps.detail: A very small lithium-polymer cell is connected to charging contacts and a protection circuit, then fitted into the remaining space.

buildSteps.title: Manufacture the titanium shell
buildSteps.detail: The outer ring is machined or moulded from titanium, then an inner plastic layer is added to hold the electronics and insulate them from skin.

buildSteps.title: Assemble and seal
buildSteps.detail: Sensors, board and battery are placed inside the shell, and the unit is sealed against sweat and water with a gasket or resin.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate each unit
buildSteps.detail: Each ring's optical and temperature sensors are individually checked so readings are consistent from device to device.

buildSteps.title: Load firmware and algorithms
buildSteps.detail: Software that filters motion noise and computes heart rate variability, sleep stages and temperature baselines is installed.

buildSteps.title: Validate accuracy
buildSteps.detail: Rings are tested against reference monitors in controlled studies to measure how closely they track heart rate and sleep.

prerequisites.why: they measure blood-volume changes using light and are small enough to fit inside a ring.
it sends data to a phone without draining the tiny battery too quickly.
they store enough energy in a few cubic centimetres to run the ring for days.
titanium and medical-grade plastics can be worn against skin continuously without irritation.

prerequisites.tech: Sleep-staging algorithms from PPG and motion
prerequisites.why: they work reasonably well for consumer trends but are not as accurate as clinical sleep studies.

pathway.milestone: consumer rings that track heart rate, HRV, sleep and skin temperature
pathway.unlocks: widespread personal health awareness and long-term trend tracking.

pathway.milestone: improved sensor accuracy and additional metrics such as blood-oxygen estimation
pathway.unlocks: more reliable detection of breathing disturbances during sleep.

pathway.milestone: regulatory clearances for specific clinical uses like sleep-apnea screening or arrhythmia alerts
pathway.unlocks: rings that can support a doctor's diagnosis, not just wellness.

pathway.milestone: integration with electronic health records and remote monitoring programmes
pathway.unlocks: continuous, passive health data that can be used in routine care.
